mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not higher than baseline during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, which may lead to negative equity returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) move in opposite directions, it indicates labor market inefficiencies, which may lead to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong economic activity, which may lead to positive equity returns as corporate earnings and revenues improve.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not higher than baseline during periods of INDPRO growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in federal funds rate signals aggressive monetary easing, which may lead to positive equity returns as liquidity increases and discount rates fall.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real consumer spending (RSAFS) signals strong demand, which may lead to positive equity returns as revenues and earnings increase.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not higher than baseline during periods of RSAFS growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate is low (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate is high (UNRATE), it indicates the economy may be in a recovery phase, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) in a late-cycle expansion may lead to negative equity returns as inflationary pressures prompt tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.
